questions.stem: Which data type stores a whole number?
questions.solution: int stores whole numbers; float stores real values.

questions.stem: How many times does a while loop execute when its condition is false initially?
questions.solution: while is a pretest loop; a false condition skips the body.

questions.stem: Which part of a for loop is executed after each iteration?
questions.solution: The update expression runs after each iteration.

questions.stem: Which statement immediately exits a loop?
questions.solution: break terminates the nearest loop or switch.

questions.stem: Which declaration creates an integer array of five elements?
questions.solution: int a[5]; reserves five integer elements.

This question tests the program development life cycle.

parts.text: Define source code and object code.
parts.answer: Source code is the human-readable program text; object code is the machine-oriented output produced by a compiler.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Describe THREE stages of the program development life cycle.
parts.answer: Analysis (requirements), design (algorithm/flowchart), coding (implementation), testing (verification), maintenance (updates). Any three stages.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correctly described stage.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A program reads three integer values and displays the largest value.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart to find the largest of three values.
parts.answer: Start -> read a, b, c -> largest = a -> if b > largest then largest = b -> if c > largest then largest = c -> display largest -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for input, initial assumption, two comparisons, output and flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the flowchart.
parts.answer: Use if statements to update largest, then cout the result.
parts.solution: Award marks for correct comparisons, variable updates and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests type conversion and constants.

parts.text: Explain the difference between implicit and explicit type conversion, and give one C++ example of each.
parts.answer: Implicit conversion is automatic (int to double); explicit conversion uses a cast such as double(total) or static_cast<double>(total).
parts.solution: Award marks for both definitions and valid examples.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a C++ program segment that calculates the average of three integer marks as a double and displays it to two decimal places.
parts.answer: double average = (m1 + m2 + m3) / 3.0; cout << fixed << setprecision(2) << average;
parts.solution: Award marks for floating-point division, fixed/setprecision and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and state the output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Rewrite the segment using a do...while loop that sums only values greater than 5.
parts.answer: int i=0,s=0; do { if(a[i]>5) s+=a[i]; i++; } while(i<5); cout<<s;
parts.solution: Award marks for do...while, condition, filter and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A class records ten student marks in an array.

parts.text: Declare an integer array of ten marks and read the marks from the user.
parts.answer: int marks[10]; for(int i=0;i<10;i++) cin >> marks[i];
parts.solution: Award marks for array declaration, loop and input.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment to calculate and display the average, highest mark and number of marks above the average.
parts.answer: Compute total and highest in one loop; average = double(total)/10; then second loop counts marks > average.
parts.solution: Award marks for total, average, highest, second loop and output.
parts.label: b
